Amplify
AM-pli-fy
verb
From Latin amplificare, to enlarge, to make greater. To amplify is to increase in volume or extent. In activist usage — 'amplify marginalized voices' — it has become a standpoint move: to give greater volume and credence to a claim not because it has been tested and found true, but because of the identity of the one who speaks it.

⚖️ Biblical Verdict

🟠
Examine
A standpoint move that credits a claim by the speaker's identity; Scripture weighs a claim by truth and tests it by witnesses, not by amplification.

📖 Biblical Definition

Scripture weighs a claim by its truth and tests it by witnesses, never by the standing of the speaker. 'He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him' (Prov. 18:17) — a matter is settled by examination, not by amplification. The command is to 'prove all things; hold fast that which is good' (1 Thess. 5:21), and the legal standard is plurality of witnesses, not volume of voice: 'at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established' (Deut. 19:15). The noble Bereans 'received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so' (Acts 17:11) — they tested even an apostle. To make a claim louder is not to make it truer; a thing amplified is merely a thing made bigger, and a lie amplified is a bigger lie. Truth is established by proof and confirmed by witnesses, not conferred by the identity of the speaker.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

'Amplify marginalized voices' — a standpoint-epistemology move; but in Scripture a claim is weighed by truth and tested by witnesses (Prov. 18:17; 1 Thess. 5:21), not amplified by the speaker's identity.

AMPLIFY, verb. To enlarge or make greater; in activist usage ('amplify marginalized voices'), to grant greater credence to a claim by the speaker's identity.

From Latin amplificare, to enlarge.

A standpoint move: volume and authority assigned by who speaks, not by whether the claim is true.

Rebutted by the biblical method: prove all things (1 Thess. 5:21), search whether they be so (Acts 17:11), establish by witnesses (Deut. 19:15) — truth tested, not amplified.

📖 Key Scripture

Proverbs 18:17 — "He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him."

1 Thessalonians 5:21 — "Prove all things; hold fast that which is good."

Acts 17:11 — "These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so."

Deuteronomy 19:15 — "One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sinneth: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established."

Proverbs 18:13 — "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him."

1 John 4:1 — "Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A standpoint move replaces the testing of a claim with the amplifying of it — volume and credence assigned by the speaker's identity; but Scripture establishes truth by proof and by witnesses, not by amplification.

expand to see more

The corruption substitutes volume for verification. 'Amplify marginalized voices' does not ask whether a claim is true; it directs that the claim be given greater credence and reach because of the identity of the one who makes it. This is standpoint epistemology in a single verb: the speaker's social position, not the evidence, becomes the warrant for belief. But amplification adds nothing to truth. To make a claim louder is to make it bigger, not better; if it is false, amplification only spreads the error farther. Scripture's instinct is the exact opposite — not 'amplify the claim' but 'search the claim': 'he that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him' (Prov. 18:17). The plausible-sounding first voice is precisely the one to be examined, not amplified. # voice-lock-ok: progressive: the standpoint command to 'amplify marginalized voices' is named here to rebut it.

The deeper error is that amplification short-circuits judgment, and judgment is a duty Scripture refuses to suspend. 'Prove all things; hold fast that which is good' (1 Thess. 5:21); 'believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God' (1 John 4:1). The Bereans were called noble for testing even Paul by the Scriptures (Acts 17:11) — not for amplifying him because of who he was, but for searching whether his words were so. To grant a claim authority by the speaker's identity is to do what Proverbs calls folly: to answer 'a matter before he heareth it' (Prov. 18:13), pronouncing on the case before it is weighed. The amplify-move dresses this folly as humility, but it is the abdication of the discernment God commands.

The recovery is to honor every person and to test every claim. Scripture is glad to give a hearing to the lowly — it commands opening the mouth for the dumb (Prov. 31:8) and forbids despising the poor man's wisdom (Eccl. 9:15-16). But a hearing is for examination, not amplification: the lowly man's claim, like the great man's, is established 'at the mouth of two witnesses' (Deut. 19:15) and proved before it is held fast (1 Thess. 5:21). To weigh a matter by its truth honors both the speaker and the truth; to amplify it by the speaker's identity honors neither, for it flatters the man and bypasses the truth. Test the claim, confirm it by witnesses, and let what is proved good stand — whoever spoke it.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin amplificare, to enlarge; an activist standpoint move that credits a claim by the speaker's identity. Scripture tests truth by proof and witnesses (Prov. 18:17; 1 Thess. 5:21; Deut. 19:15), never by amplification.

expand to see more

Latin: amplificare, to enlarge, make greater; activist usage, 'amplify marginalized voices.'

Search, don't amplify: Prov. 18:17 — the first voice that 'seemeth just' is the one to be searched, not amplified.

Test and confirm: 1 Thess. 5:21 ('prove all things') and Deut. 19:15 (two or three witnesses) — truth established, not made louder.

Usage

"To amplify a claim is to make it bigger, not truer; a lie amplified is only a bigger lie."

"The Bereans did not amplify Paul because of who he was; they searched the Scriptures whether his words were so."

"Give the lowly a hearing — then prove the matter by witnesses; volume is not verification."
